title: How many ways can two blanks give a mean of six point five?
description: Two blanks sit among the numbers three, eleven, fifteen and six, and the mean of all six must be six point five. The mean gives the total, the known numbers leave four for the blanks, and counting numbers give only a few pairs.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mean times the count gives the total, and the blanks must make up what the known numbers leave. Watch for students who count one and three and three and one as two different collections, or who allow zero.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 4)
video_script.why: A child who has found one missing value from a mean now finds how many pairs of missing values fit.
video_script.substitution: the book's numbers 3, 11, 15 and 6 with two blanks and the mean 6.5
video_script.anchor: a row of six boxes holding 3, 11, a blank, a blank, 15 and 6
video_script.payoff_line: There are two possibilities, one and three, or two and two

final_answer.spoken: there are two possibilities, one and three, or two and two

maths_rules: counting numbers start at 1: 1 + 3 = 4 and 2 + 2 = 4; 3 + 1 is the same collection as 1 + 3; 0 + 4 is not allowed
video_script.design: One row of six boxes all video, two of them blank. The mean turns into a total, the known boxes are added, and the two blanks are filled with each pair that makes up the rest.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the mean.
<bookmark mark='row'/>Six boxes hold three, eleven, two blanks, fifteen and six.
<bookmark mark='mean'/>Fill the blanks so that the mean of all six numbers is six point five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many fills are there if only counting numbers are allowed?

beats.on_screen: the row of boxes and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: total = mean × count; the blanks make up what the known numbers leave

marks.rule: the line total = mean × count appears
marks.rest: the known boxes are grouped, with the two blanks as the rest of the total

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>A mean fixes the total, because the total is the mean times the count.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The two blanks must make up whatever the known numbers leave out.

marks.given: the four known numbers, the two blanks and the mean are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers three, eleven, fifteen and six, two blanks, and a mean of six point five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the fills for the two blanks, and how many there are

marks.find: the words the fills and how many are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to fill the two blanks and count the fills.
<bookmark mark='times'/>Step one, turn the mean into the total. Multiply six point five by six.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The total of all six numbers is thirty nine.

marks.add: the four known numbers are added one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the four known numbers. Three, eleven, fifteen and six.
<bookmark mark='known'/>Their sum is thirty five.

marks.left: the two blanks must add to 4

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step three, take the known sum away from the total. Thirty nine take away thirty five leaves four.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The two blanks must add up to four.

beats.on_screen: counting numbers start at 1: 1 + 3 = 4 and 2 + 2 = 4; 3 + 1 is the same collection as 1 + 3; 0 + 4 is not allowed

marks.count: counting numbers 1, 2, 3 are listed and zero is crossed out
marks.pairs: the pairs 1 and 3, and 2 and 2, are written
marks.same: 3 and 1 is joined to 1 and 3 as the same collection

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step four, list the pairs of counting numbers that add to four. Counting numbers start at one, so zero is not allowed.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>One and three add to four, and so do two and two.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Three and one is the same collection as one and three. The order does not change the mean.

marks.one: 1 and 3 go into the blanks and 39 ÷ 6 = 6.5 is written
marks.two: 2 and 2 go into the blanks and 39 ÷ 6 = 6.5 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Check both fills. With one and three, the total is thirty nine. Thirty nine divided by six is six point five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>With two and two, the total is thirty nine again, so the mean is six point five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Two possibilities: 1 and 3, or 2 and 2
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>There are two possibilities, one and three, or two and two.
